Action Plan:
1. Dial 999 and dispatch an ambulance to patient’s home for urgent transfer to Emergency Department (ED) for suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
2. Remain on the phone with patient until paramedics arrive; provide them with collected history (onset, character, associated symptoms, risk factors).
3. Advise patient to stay seated, calm, and sip water; avoid exertion and do not self-medicate.
4. Ask patient’s wife to pack essentials and accompany him to hospital.
5. ED team to perform immediate ECG, cardiac enzymes, chest X-ray, full bloods, and continuous monitoring; cardiology consult expected on arrival.
6. Follow-up telehealth appointment to be scheduled after hospital evaluation to review results and ongoing care for chest pain, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Central chest pressure (“like someone sitting on my chest”) started suddenly 2 hours ago while gardening; constant, 7/10 intensity.  
• Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), pain radiating to left shoulder/arm. No radiation to back or head. No dysphagia, urinary, or bowel issues.  
• Recent functional decline: Increasing dyspnea on stairs/hills; intermittent calf pain and leg swelling.  
• Past medical history: Hypertension, hypercholesterolemia. No other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications: None.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Social history: Smoker. Lives at home with wife.

Objective:
• Telehealth consult—no physical examination possible; vital signs not obtained.  
• No investigation results available yet; paramedics to obtain on arrival.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Chest discomfort with suspected acute coronary syndrome  
   - Assessment: Possible ACS (unstable angina/MI).  
   - Differential diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism, aortic dissection, musculoskeletal chest wall pain.  
   - Investigations planned: Pre-hospital ECG, cardiac enzymes, chest X-ray, full blood panel, pulse oximetry, blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate.  
   - Treatment planned: Emergency ambulance transfer to ED; anticipate guideline-directed ACS protocol on arrival.  
   - Relevant referrals: ED / Cardiology.

2. Hypertension  
   - Assessment: Known hypertension, untreated.  
   - Investigations planned: Formal blood-pressure monitoring in hospital and after discharge.  
   - Treatment planned: To be reviewed post-acute event; potential initiation of antihypertensive medication once clinically stable.  
   - Relevant referrals: Primary care / Cardiology for long-term management.

3. Hypercholesterolemia  
   - Assessment: Known hyperlipidemia, untreated.  
   - Investigations planned: Fasting lipid profile (to be arranged after acute care).  
   - Treatment planned: Discuss statin therapy and lifestyle modification after hospital discharge.  
   - Relevant referrals: Primary care / Cardiology for cardiovascular risk reduction.
